result.output:
1	# Authoring `@pantoken/components`
2	
3	`@pantoken/components` is the semantic RSCSS CSS API — a parameterized generator, not hand-written
4	CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.
5	
6	## Source layout
7	
8	- `src/components/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
9	- `src/utilities/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`UTILITIES`).
10	- `src/rules/{base,prose}.ts` + `index.ts` (`RULES`).
11	- `src/declarations/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`DECLARATIONS`).
12	- `src/lib/`: `helpers.ts` (ns/scope/glyph consts/spacing scales/`ComponentOptions`/`DEFAULT_PREFIX`),
13	  `define.ts` (`defineComponent`/`defineUtility`/`defineRule`/`defineDeclaration`), `aliases.ts`
14	  (`withSizeAliases`/`withAliases`), `css.ts` (the identity `css` tag), `headings.ts`,
15	  `field-controls.ts`.
16	
17	## Authoring a record
18	
19	```ts
20	export const foo = defineComponent({
21	  name,
22	  summary,
23	  modifiers,
24	  parts,
25	  cssProperties,
26	  examples,
27	  structure,
28	  demo,
29	  css: (p) =>
30	    // prettier-ignore
31	    css`…css body…`,
32	});
33	export const fooCss = foo.css;
34	```
35	
36	- The doc comment is **metadata** — plain strings, no backtick/`${` escaping.
37	- Only the `css` body stays a template literal. **Tag it with `css` and put a `// prettier-ignore`
38	  line right before it** (before the template for a direct arrow body, before `return` for a block).
39	  oxfmt treats `css` and `styled` tagged templates as embedded CSS and corrupts interpolated
40	  selectors (`${p}foo.-mod` → `${p}foo .-mod`, a different meaning) otherwise. Setting
41	  `embeddedLanguageFormatting` to off does **not** stop it. See the engineering log.
42	- Add the record to its bucket `index.ts`. For `COMPONENTS` the order is **load-bearing** — it matches
43	  the `componentsCss()` concat order, not alphabetical.
44	
45	## The modifier convention (key-value RSCSS compound)
46	
47	- Modifiers are `.${p}<comp>.-<prop>-<val>`, aligned to InstUI prop names
48	  (`-color-secondary`, `-size-sm`, `-shape-circle`, `-variant-title-page`).
49	- Booleans are the prop name alone, presence = true (`-clickable`, `-condensed`). A default-on boolean
50	  toggled off **inverts**: `-without-background`, `-without-border`.
51	- Sizes use one scale `-size-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`, emitted with both short and long spellings as
52	  first-class aliases via `withSizeAliases()`.
53	- Nested elements are **unprefixed short classes scoped as descendants** (`.instui-menu .item`), not
54	  BEM `__`. Non-nested structural parts that can't be descendant-scoped are **flat prefixed**
55	  (`.instui-badge-wrapper`). A guard test rejects `__` and `--`.
56	- Avoid hyphen-then-digit tokens (`-2xs` needs escaping); keep tokens letter-leading.
57	
58	## Deprecated aliases (auto-discovered, always functional)
59	
60	- Author a modifier's metadata with `deprecated: "{@link -canonical}"`. `withAliases` reads that and
61	  clones each canonical rule under the alias name. There is no hardcoded pairs list.
62	- **A deprecated modifier must be a functional alias — never a doc-only noop** (user's absolute rule).
63	- The alias post-processors run on the CSS **body only**, before the doc block is prepended, because
64	  the doc block's `{@link}` braces confuse the brace-based scanners. They anchor on the base class
65	  (`.instui-radio.-variant-toggle`), not the bare token, so a bare `.-canonical` match doesn't wrongly
66	  clone `:not(.-canonical)` or compound rules.
67	
68	## `@scope` and child-combinator scoping
69	
70	`scope(root, body, children?)` (in `helpers.ts`) rewrites element rules and wraps them in
71	`@scope (root) { … }`. Two constraints that bite:
72	
73	1. Keep the component **root rule and every root-modifier-only rule (especially `-size-*`) outside**
74	   the scope, prefixed — because `withSizeAliases`/`withAliases` append twin rules at top level by
75	   scanning flat CSS; a `:scope.-size-*` twin emitted inside a scope block would be orphaned.
76	2. Never pass a body whose root token prefixes a sibling class (e.g. `.instui-progress` prefixes
77	   `.instui-progress-value`) — the string split would corrupt it to `:scope-value`. Keep flat
78	   siblings out of the scoped body.
79	
80	`@scope`/`:is`/`:has`/`:where` are **not** namespacing tools — only a unique or prefixed name prevents
81	a collision. Scoping narrows intent and deep-nesting collisions; it isn't collision-proof.
82	
83	## Icons
84	
85	Glyphs render via a single generic `[class*="${p}icon-"]::before` mask painter (currentColor, 1em
86	box). A glyph class rides a host directly because `--pantoken-glyph` is a plain (non-`@property`)
87	custom prop that inherits into `::before`. So `<button class="instui-button -shape-square
88	-icon-arrow-right">` needs no nested icon span. Built-in component glyphs source from the shared
89	`--instui-icon-<name>` tokens via an `iconMask(name)` helper.
90	
91	## Per-component checklist
92	
93	Extend the record, update the drift-checked test, update the guide (`docs/guide/components.md`), and
94	add or update a demo. Then run `vp check --fix`, the component + demo tests, `check:publish`, and
95	`lint:markdown`. Browser-verify anything visual. Skip upstream tokens that are `@property`-registered
96	but value-less (being removed upstream) — don't invent them.
97

result.output:
1	# Build, release, and the docs site
2	
3	## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly
4	
5	- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
6	[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
7	- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
8	  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
9	  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
10	  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
11	- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
12	  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.
13	
14	## The gate
15	
16	- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
17	  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
18	  `lint:js`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
19	  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
20	  race). Must pass before you're done.
21	- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
22	  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
23	  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
24	- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
25	  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
26	  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
27	  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
28	- **`publint`/`attw` are scoped to what the PR touches.** `scripts/release/changed-packages.ts` maps
29	  the diff against the base branch to the affected publishable packages (each changed package plus its
30	  workspace dependents, since a dependency change can break a dependent's pack/types), and the jobs run
31	  `vp exec -F <those>` instead of packing all ~70. A change to a global file (root `package.json`,
32	  lockfile, `vite.config.ts`, …) widens back to the full gate; a change touching no publishable package
33	  skips them.
34	- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
35	  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
36	- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
37	  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
38	  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
39	  ran on the merge-to-main the tag points at).
40	- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
41	  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
42	  creating package tags.
43	- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
44	  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
45	  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.
46	
47	See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
48	organization governance model.
49	
50	## Linting CSS
51	
52	Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
53	`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
54	`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
55	`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.
56	
57	## The docs site
58	
59	`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
60	(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
61	set a custom `i18nRouting`).
62	
63	- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
64	  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
65	  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
66	  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
67	- **Block-level API translation.** `build-api-locales.ts` doesn't translate whole `.md` files — it
68	  runs `segment-markdown.ts` to split each generated page into blocks: `prose` (descriptions,
69	  remarks, `@example` captions, cssdoc table Description cells), `glossary` (section headings,
70	  stability-badge pills, table column labels), and `preserve` (code fences, signatures, breadcrumbs,
71	  token tables). Only prose carries a content key, so a page's prose survives the scaffolding churn
72	  (badge flips, token-value changes, signature edits) that used to bust a whole-file key. `glossary`
73	  blocks always go through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (keyless, never cached);
74	  `preserve` blocks are emitted verbatim.
75	- **The committed cache carries the prose; CI serves it.** The translation memory
76	  (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and adapter-agnostic, so a claude-authored
77	  prose entry is served to a `glossary` build as a plain cache hit. The workflow: run
78	  `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` **locally** to author prose (a cold run is bounded to ~30–40
79	  batched `claude -p` calls, resumable via the memory's autosave), then commit `hu.api.json`. CI's
80	  `docs:build` runs the `glossary` adapter, which serves that prose from cache and only ever fills
81	  structural headings/labels. Brand-new prose that isn't cached yet passes through as English — the
82	  glossary **never** caches its own prose passthrough (that would permanently mask the block from a
83	  later claude run), so it stays a miss until claude authors it. Never wire `:claude` into CI.
84	- **Running the cold pass.** Each `claude -p` call cold-starts a full agent, and the dominant cost is
85	  the per-call bootstrap — loading MCP servers, plugins, and project settings — not the translation
86	  itself (it dwarfs even a small model's inference). So the `:claude` tasks pass
87	  `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user`: a fast model, **no
88	  MCP**, and user settings only (keeps auth, drops project/local hooks). That cuts each call from
89	  minutes to a few seconds. Override by editing the task or exporting your own
90	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` before a direct `node scripts/…` run (`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`
91	  overrides the `claude` binary itself). Either task logs progress (`… N/M labels + prose blocks
92	translated`) and saves the memory after **each** chunk, so it's resumable — a kill or crash keeps
93	  completed chunks and a re-run serves them from cache.
94	- **The cold pass is generation-bound, so it runs chunks concurrently.** Once MCP is stripped, the
95	  wall-clock cost is the model streaming translations, not startup — so `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter`
96	  runs up to `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 5) `claude -p` calls at once. Prose is batched at
97	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_BATCH_BUDGET` chars/request (default 4k) — small enough that each JSON response
98	  stays reliable and progress is fine-grained, with the pool hiding the per-call startup. A chunk that
99	  errors is logged and skipped (its blocks stay uncached and retry next run), never sinking the whole
100	  run. Raise concurrency for more speed if you're not rate-limited; lower the budget if a run trips the
101	  per-item fallback (the model dropping a key from a large response).
102	
103	## The cssdoc integration
104	
105	pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
106	workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
107	(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
108	and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
109	`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
110	`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.
111	
112	**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
113	catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.
114	
115	## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation
116	
117	Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
118	that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
119	direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:
120	
121	- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
122	  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
123	- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
124	- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
125	  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
126	  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.
127	
128	A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
129	script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.
130

1	/**
2	 * The `--instui-elevation-*` shadow scale. Helpers only — NOT a documented record and not in any
3	 * registry: `componentsCss()` leads its sheet with `elevationCss()` so the shadows components
4	 * reference (modal, alert, menu) resolve from `components.css` alone.
5	 *
6	 * @module
7	 */
8	
9	/** Per-level geometry (`offset-x offset-y blur`) for the [tighter, wider] shadow layers. */
10	const ELEVATION_GEOMETRY: Record<string, [tight: string, wide: string]> = {
11	  resting: ["0 0.0625rem 0.125rem", "0 0.0625rem 0.1875rem"],
12	  above: ["0 0.1875rem 0.375rem", "0 0.1875rem 0.375rem"],
13	  topmost: ["0 0.375rem 0.4375rem", "0 0.625rem 1.75rem"],
14	};
15	
16	/** Aliases InstUI ships alongside the primary level names. */
17	const ELEVATION_ALIASES: Record<string, keyof typeof ELEVATION_GEOMETRY> = {
18	  depth1: "resting",
19	  depth2: "above",
20	  depth3: "topmost",
21	  card: "resting",
22	  cardHover: "topmost",
23	};
24	
25	/**
26	 * Every elevation level and alias emitted as `--instui-elevation-<name>` (`resting`, `above`,
27	 * `topmost`, `depth1`–`depth3`, `card`, `cardHover`). Derived from the geometry + alias maps.
28	 */
29	export const ELEVATION_NAMES: readonly string[] = [
30	  ...Object.keys(ELEVATION_GEOMETRY),
31	  ...Object.keys(ELEVATION_ALIASES),
32	];
33	
34	// The tighter layer takes the softer colour, the wider layer the stronger one — InstUI's "lifted" look.
35	const ELEVATION_COLOR_STRONG = "var(--instui-color-drop-shadow-shadow-color1)";
36	const ELEVATION_COLOR_SOFT = "var(--instui-color-drop-shadow-shadow-color2)";
37	const elevationShadow = ([tight, wide]: [string, string]): string =>
38	  `${tight} ${ELEVATION_COLOR_SOFT}, ${wide} ${ELEVATION_COLOR_STRONG}`;
39	
40	/**
41	 * The `--instui-elevation-*` name/value pairs (each a multi-layer `box-shadow`). Values reference the
42	 * themed drop-shadow colour tokens, so they adapt per theme wherever a token sheet is loaded.
43	 *
44	 * @returns One `[customProperty, value]` pair per level and alias.
45	 */
46	export function elevationDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
47	  const levels: [string, [string, string]][] = [
48	    ...Object.entries(ELEVATION_GEOMETRY),
49	    ...Object.entries(ELEVATION_ALIASES).map(([alias, base]): [string, [string, string]] => [
50	      alias,
51	      ELEVATION_GEOMETRY[base],
52	    ]),
53	  ];
54	  return levels.map(([name, geo]) => [`--instui-elevation-${name}`, elevationShadow(geo)]);
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Build the elevation token block: `<selector> { --instui-elevation-*: … }`. Shipped inside
59	 * `components.css` (so shadows are intrinsic — no plugin, no extra import), and reusable by other
60	 * layered outputs (e.g. the Pendo renderer) via the `selector` option.
61	 *
62	 * @param options - `selector` — the rule selector (default `:root`).
63	 * @returns The CSS string.
64	 *
65	 * @example
66	 * ```ts
67	 * import { elevationCss } from "@pantoken/components";
68	 *
69	 * elevationCss(); // ":root { --instui-elevation-resting: …; --instui-elevation-above: …; … }"
70	 * ```
71	 *
72	 * @demo self:elevation
73	 */
74	export function elevationCss(options: { selector?: string } = {}): string {
75	  const selector = options.selector ?? ":root";
76	  const body = elevationDeclarations()
77	    .map(([name, value]) => `  ${name}: ${value};`)
78	    .join("\n");
79	  return `${selector} {\n${body}\n}\n`;
80	}
81

2	 * The focus-outline system — the InstUI focus ring, intrinsic to `base.css` so every focusable gets it
3	 * out of the box when pantoken owns the page. The resting element carries a transparent ring + a
4	 * transition, and `:focus-visible` reveals the colour and grows the offset. All rules are
5	 * zero-specificity `:where()`, so any component style overrides without `!important`.
6	 *
7	 * This is the one documented `@declaration` record, but it can't use `defineDeclaration` (its CSS is a
8	 * token block on one selector plus ring rules on another). Instead it exposes {@link focusOutlineCss}
9	 * (the bespoke builder `base.css` calls directly) and a {@link Definition}-shaped {@link focus} object
10	 * so the registry + `validate()` can treat it uniformly.
11	 *
12	 * @module
13	 */
14	import { css } from "../lib/css.ts";
15	import type { Definition } from "../lib/define.ts";
16	
17	/** The focus declaration's cssdoc doc comment (authored inline; the CSS body follows in {@link focusOutlineCss}). */
18	// prettier-ignore
19	const FOCUS_DOC = css`/**
20	 * @declaration focus
21	 * @class :focus-visible
22	 * @summary The focus-outline system: the \`--instui-focus-outline-*\` custom properties (declared on \`:root\`) plus the \`:focus-visible\` ring every focusable gets, and opt-in tuning classes.
23	 * @modifier -focus-color-success — Success-coloured ring.
24	 * @modifier -focus-color-danger — Danger-coloured ring.
25	 * @modifier -focus-color-inverse — Inverse (on-dark) ring.
26	 * @modifier -focus-position-inset — Draw the ring inset, inside the element's edge.
27	 * @modifier -focus-within — Ring the element while a descendant is focused.
28	 * @modifier -without-focus-animation — Disable the ring's grow-in animation.
29	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color — The ring colour once focus is visible (the themed info colour).
30	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-start — The resting, transparent ring colour the outline transitions from.
31	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-width — The outline width of the ring.
32	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-offset — The gap between the element's edge and the ring when focused.
33	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-radius — The ring's corner radius when focused.
34	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-style — The outline line style (solid).
35	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-transition — The transition that animates the ring's colour and offset in.
36	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-success — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-success\` modifier.
37	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-danger — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-danger\` modifier.
38	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-inverse — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-inverse\` (on-dark) modifier.
39	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-inset — The outline offset used when \`-focus-position-inset\` draws the ring inside the edge.
40	 * @a11y Every focusable element gets a \`:focus-visible\` outline ring so keyboard users can see what's focused.
41	 * @example
42	 * <button class="instui-button -focus-color-danger">Delete</button>
43	 * @demo self:focus-outline
44	 */`;
45	
46	/** The elements the ring applies to by default (the common interactive/focusable elements). */
47	export const FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR = "a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]";

50	  `var(--instui-component-shared-tokens-focus-outline-${name})`;

55	 *
56	 * @returns One `[customProperty, value]` pair per focus-ring variable.
57	 */
58	export function focusOutlineDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
59	  return [
60	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color", focusShared("info-color")],
61	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-start", "transparent"],
62	    ["--instui-focus-outline-width", focusShared("width")],
63	    ["--instui-focus-outline-offset", focusShared("offset")],
64	    ["--instui-focus-outline-radius", "var(--instui-border-radius-md)"],
65	    ["--instui-focus-outline-style", "solid"],
66	    ["--instui-focus-outline-transition", "outline-color 0.2s, outline-offset 0.25s"],
67	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-success", focusShared("success-color")],
68	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-danger", focusShared("danger-color")],
69	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse", focusShared("on-color")],
70	    ["--instui-focus-outline-inset", "0rem"],

74	/**
75	 * The focus-ring rules for a given focusable selector: a transparent resting ring that transitions in
76	 * on `:focus-visible`, plus the `-focus-color-*` / `-focus-position-inset` / `-focus-within` /
77	 * `-without-focus-animation` modifiers. All `:where()`-wrapped, so zero-specificity.
78	 *
79	 * @param selector - The focusable selector the base ring applies to (default {@link FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR}).
80	 * @returns The CSS rules string.
81	 */
82	export function focusOutlineRules(selector: string = FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR): string {
83	  return [
84	    `:where(${selector}) {`,
85	    `  outline: var(--instui-focus-outline-width) var(--instui-focus-outline-style) var(--instui-focus-outline-color-start);`,
86	    `  outline-offset: 0;`,
87	    `  transition: var(--instui-focus-outline-transition);`,
88	    `}`,
89	    `:where(${selector}):where(:focus-visible) {`,
90	    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
91	    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
92	    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
93	    `}`,
94	    `:where(.-focus-color-success):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-success); }`,
95	    `:where(.-focus-color-danger):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-danger); }`,
96	    `:where(.-focus-color-inverse):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse); }`,
97	    `:where(.-focus-position-inset):where(:focus-visible) { outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-inset); }`,
98	    `:where(.-focus-within):where(:focus-within) {`,
99	    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
100	    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
101	    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
102	    `}`,
103	    `:where(.-without-focus-animation) { transition: none; }`,
104	  ].join("\n");
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * Build the focus-outline block: the `--instui-focus-outline-*` token defs plus the ring rules.
109	 * Baked into `base.css` (so focusables get the ring out of the box), and reusable by other layered
110	 * outputs (e.g. the Pendo renderer) via the `selector`/`tokenSelector` options.
111	 *
112	 * @param options - `selector` — the focusable selector; `tokenSelector` — where the token defs land
113	 *   (default `:where(:root)`).
114	 * @returns The CSS string.
115	 *
116	 * @demo self:focus-outline
117	 */
118	export function focusOutlineCss(
119	  options: { selector?: string; tokenSelector?: string } = {},
120	): string {
121	  const tokenSelector = options.tokenSelector ?? ":where(:root)";
122	  const decls = focusOutlineDeclarations()
123	    .map(([name, value]) => `  ${name}: ${value};`)
124	    .join("\n");
125	  // prettier-ignore
126	  return css`${FOCUS_DOC}\n${tokenSelector} {\n${decls}\n}\n\n${focusOutlineRules(options.selector)}\n`;
127	}
128	
129	/**
130	 * The {@link Definition}-shaped view of the focus declaration, so it can sit in the DECLARATIONS
131	 * registry and be checked by `validate()`. `css()`/`rules()` delegate to {@link focusOutlineCss} (its
132	 * default `instui`-prefixed output is a single well-formed declaration record).
133	 */
134	export const focus: Definition = {
135	  name: "focus",
136	  kind: "declaration",
137	  rules: () => focusOutlineCss(),
138	  css: () => focusOutlineCss(),
139	};

11	/** Options for {@link iconGlyphsCss}. */
12	export interface IconGlyphsOptions extends ComponentOptions {
13	  /**
14	   * Also emit the deprecated InstUI-prop glyph aliases (`-render-icon-<name>`, `-render-custom-icon-<name>`)
15	   * as functional aliases of `-icon-<name>`. Off by default — turning it on roughly doubles the sheet, so
16	   * enable it only when you need markup written against the old `renderIcon`/`renderCustomIcon` prop names

18	   */

20	}

22	/**
23	 * Build the icon-glyph stylesheet: one `.<prefix>-icon-<name>` class per icon that points
24	 * `--pantoken-glyph` at the matching `--instui-icon-<name>` token. Kept out of the component bundle
25	 * (it's large); ships as its own `icons.css`. Pass the icon names (e.g. from `@pantoken/icons`).
26	 *
27	 * @param names - Icon names without the `--instui-icon-` prefix (e.g. `["megaphone", "check"]`).
28	 * @param options - {@link IconGlyphsOptions} (adds `deprecatedAliases` to {@link ComponentOptions}).
29	 * @returns The CSS string.
30	 *
31	 * @example
32	 * ```ts
33	 * import { iconGlyphsCss } from "@pantoken/components";
34	 * import { icons } from "@pantoken/icons";
35	 *
36	 * const css = iconGlyphsCss(icons.map((i) => i.name)); // .-icon-megaphone { --pantoken-glyph: … }
37	 * ```
38	 *
39	 * This is the glyph-token half of the icon system (the `.-icon-<name>` modifiers, shipped as
40	 * `icons.css`); the `icon` utility is the painter half (the shared `::before`). They share the `icon`
41	 * demo.
42	 */
43	export function iconGlyphsCss(names: readonly string[], options: IconGlyphsOptions = {}): string {
44	  const prefix = options.prefix || "";
45	  const p = ns(prefix);
46	  void p; // glyph classes are prefix-independent modifiers (.-icon-<name>); consumed by any host.
47	  // The deprecated InstUI prop names that normalized to `-icon-<name>` (Pill's `renderIcon`, Alert's
48	  // `renderCustomIcon`). When `deprecatedAliases` is on, they're grouped onto the same rule as
49	  // FUNCTIONAL aliases (they set the same glyph var, and both contain the `-icon-` substring so the
50	  // shared painter + Alert's glyph pipe already fire) — otherwise omitted, which roughly halves the
51	  // sheet. They're `@deprecated` in each component's doc comment either way.
52	  const prefixes = options.deprecatedAliases
53	    ? ["-icon", "-render-icon", "-render-custom-icon"]
54	    : ["-icon"];
55	  const selectors = (name: string): string => prefixes.map((pre) => `.${pre}-${name}`).join(", ");
56	  const rules = names

58	    .join("\n");
59	  return `/* InstUI icon glyphs (@pantoken/components) — prefix: ${prefix} */\n${rules}\n`;
60	}

content.text:
I now have a complete, authoritative picture from all three explorations plus my own reads. Here's what the sweep found, before I lock scope with you.

## Findings

**Q4 — Is `plugins/pantoken/stacking` dead code? No.** It's not dead and it isn't superseded by elevation. They're orthogonal: stacking emits `z-index` tokens (`--instui-stacking-*`) plus `.instui-stack-*` utility classes from InstUI's View stacking scale; elevation emits `box-shadow` tokens (`--instui-elevation-*`). Different property, different namespace. Stacking is fully wired — re-exported by the `@pantoken` aggregate (namespace + `./stacking` subpath), depended on by `packages/pantoken` and `docs`, consumed by `docs/scripts/demos.ts` to emit `stacking.css`, and covered by its own tests. Removing it would break the aggregate. **No action — keep it.**

**Q1 — What lacks cssdoc?** Inside `formats/components`, coverage is already complete — every record carries a block and the `cssdoc/valid-doc-comments` linter enforces `missing-summary` / `undocumented-modifier` / `undocumented-part`. The genuinely undocumented CSS emitters are the **plugins** (`stacking`, `transition`, `visual-debug`, `logos`, `primitives`) — they ship user-facing classes with zero cssdoc, and none is in the lint globs or the docs CSS-API pipeline. Plus `declarations/elevation.ts` (a helper, intentionally undocumented). Intentionally excluded and best left: `select` (experimental base-select), `icon-glyphs` (shares the documented `icon` painter's demo).

**Q2 — What's incomplete?** The linter is the ground truth here, and it runs in the `ready` gate + CI over `formats/components/generated/*.css` and the co-located `.css`. On this clean branch that gate is green, so there are no *known* incomplete blocks in the validated set. The latent gap is that plugin CSS is unvalidated — nothing enforces completeness there.

**Q3 — What can be externalized like the components model?** Only `rules/base.ts` is a clean fit — it's fully static, zero interpolation, so it maps exactly onto the `.css` + 3-line-wrapper model (needs `rules/` added to the codegen `sources` array). Everything else that still holds inline `css\`\`` is a *parameterized generator* — the 7 `.ts` components interpolate runtime values (`alpha`/`darken` color math, shared `fieldControlBase`/`headingLevelRules` fragments, glyph data-URIs), and view/spacing/layout/responsive build rules from JS loops. Those can't become static `.css` — which is exactly why the codegen `sources` is limited to `components/` + `utilities/` today.

A few scope decisions are genuinely yours before I write the plan.

## Context you must verify by reading

**The cssdoc/components model** (`formats/components/`):
- `.css` files under `src/{components,utilities}/` are the authoring source; each opens with a `/** @component|@utility|@rule|@declaration <name> ... @summary ... */` cssdoc block, using the `pfx-` class-prefix SENTINEL. `scripts/component-styles.ts` codegens them into `src/generated/component-styles.ts` string consts (retaining doc comments). The rule is `@cssdoc/valid-doc-comments` (config in root `cssdoc.jsonc`), which enforces `@summary`, `undocumented-modifier`, `undocumented-part`, etc.

It reads `formats/components/generated/{components,utilities,prose,base}.css`, parses records with `parseCssDocs`, resolves `--instui-*` tokens, and writes `docs/api/css/**` pages + merges a sidebar section. Read this file fully — it's the integration point.

**The plugins** (`plugins/pantoken/*/src/index.ts`): each is a `@pantoken/plugin-*` package with a `definePlugin({ name, tokens?, css? })`. The `css` hook returns `{ marker, declarations?, append|prepend: rulesString }`. Currently emit user-facing classes with NO cssdoc:

- `visual-debug` — `-with-visual-debug` compound modifier.
- `logos` — logo classes; has a static `generated/logos.css`.
- `primitives` — `.instui-bg-primitive-color-*`; has a static `generated/primitives.css`.

# CSS documentation + externalization sweep

## Context

`formats/components/src/{declarations,lib,rules,utilities}` and `plugins/pantoken/*` all emit CSS.
This sweep answers four questions about that surface: what needs a cssdoc block, what blocks are
incomplete, what inline template-literal CSS can be externalized to the `.css`-file model, and whether
`plugins/pantoken/stacking` is dead code. The exploration produced clear, sometimes surprising answers —
one premise (stacking is dead) is false, and the components package is already fully documented — so the
actual work concentrates on the plugins plus two small, high-value changes.

### What the sweep found (the answers)

- **Q4 — `plugins/pantoken/stacking` is NOT dead code.** It emits `z-index` tokens (`--instui-stacking-*`)
  and `.instui-stack-*` utility classes from InstUI's View stacking scale. `declarations/elevation` emits
  `box-shadow` tokens (`--instui-elevation-*`) — a different property, namespace, and concern. Stacking is
  fully wired: re-exported by the `@pantoken` aggregate (namespace + `./stacking` subpath), a dependency of
  `packages/pantoken` and `docs`, consumed by `docs/scripts/demos.ts` to emit `stacking.css`, and covered by
  its own tests. **No action — removing it would break the aggregate package.**
- **Q1/Q2 — Inside `formats/components`, cssdoc coverage is already complete and gate-enforced.** Every record
  carries a block; `@cssdoc/valid-doc-comments` (in the `ready` gate + CI over `generated/*.css` and the
  co-located source `.css`) enforces `@summary` and flags `undocumented-modifier`/`undocumented-part`. On this
  green branch there are no known-incomplete blocks in the validated set. The genuinely **undocumented,
  unvalidated** CSS is `plugins/pantoken/*` (see below) and the `elevation` helper.
- **Q3 — Only `rules/base.ts` is a clean externalization fit.** Everything else still holding inline `css\`\``
  is a parameterized generator (runtime color math, shared fragments, JS-loop-built rules) that cannot become
  static `.css` — which is exactly why the codegen `sources` is limited to `components/` + `utilities/`.

## Work items

### 1. Bring `plugins/pantoken/*` into cssdoc — docs + lint + API pages (full scope)

_(Filled in from the plugin-integration design — see section below once the Plan agent returns.)_

### 2. Promote `elevation` to a documented `@declaration` record

Mirror the `focus` declaration exactly. `declarations/focus.ts` is the template: a static `FOCUS_DOC` cssdoc
block (`css\`/** @declaration focus ... */\``), a bespoke builder that prepends it, and a `Definition`-shaped
object registered in `DECLARATIONS`.

- **`formats/components/src/declarations/elevation.ts`**
  - Add an `ELEVATION_DOC` `css\`\`` block: `@declaration elevation`, `@summary`, one `@cssproperty
    --instui-elevation-<name>` per level/alias (resting, above, topmost, depth1–3, card, cardHover),
    `@related view` (the `view -shadow-*` modifiers consume it), `@demo self:elevation` (the
    `docs/demos/elevation.html` demo already exists), and an `@a11y`/`@remarks` note if useful.
  - Prepend `ELEVATION_DOC` in `elevationCss()` output (as `focusOutlineCss` prepends `FOCUS_DOC`), so the
    block leads `components.css` and flows into lint + `build-css-api`. Keep the `selector` option working.
  - Add a `Definition`-shaped `elevation` export (`kind: "declaration"`, `rules`/`css` delegating to
    `elevationCss()`), like `focus` at the bottom of `focus.ts`.
- **`formats/components/src/declarations/index.ts`** — add `elevation` to `DECLARATIONS` (`[focus, elevation]`)
  and update the module comment (it currently says elevation is "deliberately excluded").
- **`formats/components/tests/parity.test.ts:20`** — `DECLARATIONS.length` `1` → `2`.

# Design: bring `plugins/pantoken/*` CSS into the cssdoc system

## What I verified

**The proven pattern already exists in-repo.** `formats/components/scripts/generate.ts` (lines 134-147) authors a cssdoc block for a *generated* utility whose emitted classes are `.instui-*`, not `pfx-`:

```
/**
 * @utility color
 * @class .instui-text-danger
 * @summary Semantic colour utilities: `.instui-bg-<name>`, ...
 * @example <p class="instui-text-danger">...</p>
 */
```

It prepends this to `colorUtilitiesCss(...)` and writes the whole thing into `generated/utilities.css`. That single record:
- lint-validates because `generated/*.css` is in the `lint:css`/`lint:js` globs (root `vite.config.ts` lines 77, 82),
- feeds `build-css-api.ts` because it reads `formats/components/generated/utilities.css`,
- covers *hundreds* of sibling `.instui-bg-*`/`.instui-text-*`/`.instui-stroke-*` classes under one `@utility` record, with `@class` naming a representative.

This resolves the two hardest questions up front:
- **The SENTINEL/prefix problem is a non-issue.** Plugin sheets are emitted at the fixed `instui` prefix and never re-prefixed by a consumer's `raw.replaceAll(SENTINEL, p)`, so they carry no `pfx-` sentinel. cssdoc associates the doc comment with the immediately-following rules and uses `@class` to name the canonical selector — exactly as the `color` utility does. No sentinel needed.
- **`@utility` + `@class` is the record kind.** The RECORD regex in `build-css-api.ts` (`@(?:component|utility|rule|declaration)`, lines 155, 181) and the shipping `color` record both confirm `@utility` parses and renders today.

**Gitignore reality (important for ordering):** `.gitignore` ignores `**/generated/`. NONE of the generated sheets are committed — `formats/components/generated/*.css` and the existing `plugins/pantoken/{logos,primitives}/generated/*.css` are all reproduced by `vp run -r build` (the `build:all` node). So `build-css-api` already depends on `build:all` having run first (true in CI; `docs:dev` additionally runs `@pantoken/components#generate`). Plugin sheets slot into this exact model.

**Two plugin shapes:**
- `logos`, `primitives` already have `scripts/generate.ts` + committed-shape `generated/*.css` + a static `./x.css` export + are already in `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`. They only lack a cssdoc block.
- `stacking`, `transition`, `visual-debug` build rules inline in JS, have no generate script, no generated sheet, and export only `.` — they need the full generate/pack/export scaffold (mirroring `primitives`).

## Design decisions

1. **Where the doc block lives:** author it in each plugin's `scripts/generate.ts` (not in `src/index.ts`), so it never bloats the runtime `toCss` output — matching the `color` precedent. `generate.ts` composes `:root{declarations}` + doc block + rules and writes `generated/<name>.css`. The doc block must sit *immediately before* the class rules (cssdoc binds a comment to the next rule), so the `:root` declarations block goes *first*, then doc, then the `.instui-*` rules.

2. **Node-free constraint respected:** the doc/composition logic lives in `scripts/generate.ts` (a build script, not in `files`), which may use `node:fs` — exactly as `logos`/`primitives` already do. `src/index.ts` stays Node-free. To let `generate.ts` compose without duplicating the rules, export the module-level `rules` string (and a small declarations accessor) from each plugin `src/index.ts` — these are plain strings, still Node-free.

3. **Feeding `build-css-api.ts`: a second `emitCssApi` call.** `emitCssApi`'s `mergeCssSidebar` *replaces the section with the same label* and preserves others, so a second call with a distinct `label` (e.g. `"CSS plugins"`) and its own `outSubdir`/`baseHref` cleanly appends a second section while keeping the existing `"CSS"` section. A second call is preferable to extending the single `css[]` array because every plugin-specific hook diverges from the component path:
   - `importSnippet` must emit `@import "@pantoken/plugin-stacking/stacking.css";`, not `@pantoken/components/...`,
   - `resolveSource` must point at the plugin's `scripts/generate.ts` (its own `sourceMap`),
   - `resolveToken`/`localVars` must be rebuilt from the plugin sheets so `--instui-stacking-*` and `--instui-transition-*` resolve (they're defined in each sheet's `:root`, so the existing `matchAll(/(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*.../)` localVars scan picks them up once the plugin sheets are in the scanned string),
   - the drift guard `unknownReferences(css, tokens)` (lines 269-274) would flag `--instui-stacking-*`, `--instui-transition-*`, `--pantoken-visual-debug-color` — a second call keeps that guard scoped to component sheets only, avoiding widening the allow-filter.

   (Alternative if a *unified* "CSS" section is wanted: keep one call, add plugin sheets to `sheets`/`cssPaths`, add a name→package map for `importSnippet`, include plugin generate scripts in `componentSources`, and extend the drift-guard prefix filter to allow `--instui-stacking-`, `--instui-transition-`, `--pantoken-`. More branching, one section.)

4. **Lint globs:** add `"plugins/pantoken/*/generated/*.css"` to both `lint:css` and `lint:js` in root `vite.config.ts` (lines 76-83). Both tasks already `dependsOn: ["build:all"]`, and each plugin's `build` will run its `generate` (see below), so the sheets exist before lint runs — same "generate exactly once through build:all" guarantee noted in that file. No new race.

**A. Runtime-only plugins (`stacking`, `transition`, `visual-debug`) — add the generate scaffold**

Model file: `plugins/pantoken/primitives/scripts/generate.ts`. 4. `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}/package.json` — add `"generate": "node scripts/generate.ts"` and a static `"./<name>.css": "./dist/<name>.css"` export (mirror `primitives`).

**B. Already-generated plugins (`logos`, `primitives`) — add the doc block only**

5. `plugins/pantoken/logos/scripts/generate.ts` and `plugins/pantoken/primitives/scripts/generate.ts` — prepend a `@utility` doc block (with a representative `@class`, e.g. `.instui-bg-primitive-color-aurora-aurora10` for primitives) to the emitted sheet before writing. No new export/task needed — they already ship the sheet and are in `validate-generated`.

**D. Docs CSS-API**

In CI (`docs:build` → `build-api-locales.ts`) the plugin sheets come from `build:all`, so CI is fine; for `docs:dev` freshness, add the three plugin `#generate` runs (or rely on a prior `build:all`). # CSS documentation + externalization sweep

## Context

`formats/components/src/{declarations,lib,rules,utilities}` and `plugins/pantoken/*` all emit CSS.
This sweep answers four questions about that surface: what needs a cssdoc block, what blocks are
incomplete, what inline template-literal CSS can be externalized to the `.css`-file model, and whether
`plugins/pantoken/stacking` is dead code. The exploration produced clear, sometimes surprising answers —
one premise (stacking is dead) is false, and the components package is already fully documented — so the
actual work concentrates on the plugins plus two small, high-value changes.

### What the sweep found (the answers)

CI is fully green — every check passes. Now the release. I've determined the best-practice flow is **merge to main, then run the `cut-release.ts` orchestrator** (`vpr release`) on main: it computes the dependency-aware set, re-runs scoped gates, bumps, tags, and pushes — and the tag push triggers `release.yml` to publish. ## Summary

**The work (PR [#7](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/7), merged):** five commits documenting the CSS-emitting code — plugin cssdoc records with lint enforcement and new "CSS plugins" API pages, `elevation` promoted to a documented `@declaration`, `base.ts` externalized to `base.css`, plus the Hungarian translation for the new pages/sidebar. **The release (all 6 requested, best-practice flow = merge → orchestrate on main):** `@pantoken/components@0.1.1` and the five plugins at `0.1.1`, cascading via the dependency-aware set to 17 packages total (the `@pantoken/pantoken` aggregate at `0.1.3` and components' dependents — angular, cli `0.1.2`, drupal, hugo, jekyll, pendo, react, svelte, vue, web-components). All live on npm and verified.

**Three release-pipeline bugs I hit and worked around — worth a proper fix on your side:**

1. **`cut-release.ts` commit message** uses a `release:` type (not in your commitlint allowlist) with a 211-char header (max 100). Its `git commit` is rejected, so `vpr release` can't complete on its own. I committed the bumps manually with a valid `chore:` message. *Fix: change the message to `chore(release): …` and shorten the header.*
2. **`release.yml` regenerated unformatted `.release-plan.json/.md`** then failed its own `vp check` gate — before npm publish. *I fixed this in `37c63c9`: gitignored the ephemeral `.release-plan.*` / `.release-packages.txt` artifacts so `vp check` skips them (they're regenerated every run).* This also means `cut-release.ts`'s `git add .release-plan.json` will now need `-f` or removal.
3. **Multi-tag pushes don't auto-trigger `release.yml`** (GitHub's multi-tag-push limit), and `workflow_dispatch` runs all share the `refs/heads/main` concurrency group, so parallel dispatches **cancel each other**. I published via `workflow_dispatch` one at a time. *Fix: key concurrency on `inputs.package_tag` for the dispatch path, or push tags individually.*

The 6 tags remain at `2fa3bdb`; the two follow-up fix commits are on top. The earlier `422 repository.url` provenance failure did not recur — the `gate:repository` check is holding.

The packages had published, but no GitHub Releases appeared because `release.yml`'s **Create GitHub release** step is gated `if: github.event_name == 'push'` — it only runs on tag pushes, not `workflow_dispatch`. Since GitHub's multi-tag-push limit meant I had to trigger every publish via `workflow_dispatch`, that step was skipped on all 6 runs.

- [@pantoken/components@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/components@v0.1.1) — notes cover the full 12-package dependency set
- [@pantoken/plugin-stacking@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/plugin-stacking@v0.1.1)
- [@pantoken/plugin-transition@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/plugin-transition@v0.1.1)
- [@pantoken/plugin-visual-debug@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/plugin-visual-debug@v0.1.1)
- [@pantoken/plugin-logos@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/plugin-logos@v0.1.1)
- [@pantoken/plugin-primitives@v0.1.1](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/releases/tag/@pantoken/plugin-primitives@v0.1.1)

Combined with the concurrency-group fix I noted earlier (key it on `inputs.package_tag`, not `github.ref`), the dispatch path would fully match the tag-push path.

Fixes the release-pipeline bugs surfaced while cutting the `v0.1.1` CSS-cssdoc release, which forced a fully manual publish + release-notes path.

## Bugs fixed

**`release.yml`**
- **GitHub releases skipped on `workflow_dispatch`.** The *Create GitHub release* step was gated `if: github.event_name == 'push'`. Because GitHub caps how many workflow runs a single multi-tag push creates, a 6-tag release had to be dispatched — so every package published to npm but no GitHub release or notes were cut. - **`git add`ed gitignored artifacts.** `.release-plan.*` / `.release-packages.txt` are now gitignored (regenerated by `release.yml` each run), so they're no longer staged.

## Not included (follow-ups)
- The publish step still errors if a version is already on npm (re-running a tag fails instead of skipping). Left as-is to keep this change focused.

# Proposal to send upstream to cssdoc: custom sidebar/index groups

## Context

pantoken's docs CSS-API (`docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`) renders two `emitCssApi` sections —
`"CSS"` (components/utilities/rules/declarations) and `"CSS plugins"` (the plugin records). We want
the plugin records to appear **inside** the CSS section as a fifth subsection, so the CSS nav reads
`Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`.

cssdoc can't express that today: sidebar/index grouping is hardcoded to the four record **kinds**, and
the only way to get a distinct plugin group is a second top-level `emitCssApi` section. The clean fix is
a small, general cssdoc feature — so **instead of post-processing pantoken's sidebar JSON, we send cssdoc
a proposal**. This plan's deliverable is that proposal document (below), ready to file as a cssdoc issue
/ discussion. pantoken adopts it once cssdoc ships (see "Follow-up").

### Verified cssdoc internals (v0.7.8) the proposal builds on

- `KIND_GROUPS` in `@cssdoc/markdown/dist/index.mjs` — `[{kind:"component",label:"Components"}, {utility→Utilities}, {rule→Rules}, {declaration→Declarations}]`. Consumed **identically** by `buildSidebar` (sidebar tree) and `renderIndex` (index page) — both do `entries.filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, in fixed array order, dropping empty groups. No sort/label/order override.
- `@group`/`@category` — a `block` tag in `@cssdoc/spec` (`category` aliases `group`); parsed into `CssDocEntry.group?: string` in `@cssdoc/core`. **Currently used only** by `renderEntry` for the per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line — it does NOT touch sidebar/index grouping. So it's free to repurpose.
- `EmitCssApiOptions` (`@cssdoc/typedoc`) extends `RenderEntryOptions`; `mergeCssSidebar(existing, label, cssItems)` replaces the top-level node whose `text === label`. `RenderConfig` (`@cssdoc/config`) = `sectionOrder`/`headingPrefix`/`baseHref`/`structureView`, `additionalProperties:false` (a new option needs a schema addition, mirroring how `sectionOrder`/`structureView` already thread through).
- Public symbols the proposal names: `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex`, `KIND_GROUPS` (`@cssdoc/markdown`); `emitCssApi`, `EmitCssApiOptions` (`@cssdoc/typedoc`); `RenderConfig`, `cssDocSchema` (`@cssdoc/config`); `CssDocEntry.group` (`@cssdoc/core`).

---

## Deliverable: the proposal document (ready to send)

> Save verbatim to `docs/internal/proposals/cssdoc-custom-groups.md` (new dir) and/or file it as an
> issue on the cssdoc repo. Written to cssdoc's maintainers, so it references their symbols directly.

---

### Proposal: group sidebar & index by `@group`, not only by record kind

**cssdoc version reviewed:** 0.7.8

#### Summary

Let CSS records opt into a named sidebar/index group via the existing `@group`/`@category` tag, instead
of always grouping by the four record kinds. Records without `@group` are unchanged. This is a small,
backward-compatible change in `@cssdoc/markdown`, and it removes the need for consumers to emit a second
top-level `emitCssApi` section (or post-process the sidebar) just to get a custom group.

#### Motivation

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` group records solely by `record.kind` via the hardcoded `KIND_GROUPS`
array. A consumer that wants an extra section — e.g. a **Plugins** group holding records of mixed kinds
(some `@utility`, some `@declaration`) — has no supported way to do it within one section. The only
workarounds are:

1. A **second `emitCssApi` call** with a different `label` → a separate *top-level* sidebar section
   (`mergeCssSidebar` keys on `label`), which is a sibling of the main CSS section, not a child of it.
2. **Post-processing the emitted `typedoc-sidebar.json`** to splice the second section's items back in as
   a subgroup — brittle and outside cssdoc's contract.

pantoken hits exactly this: we document five CSS-emitting plugins (stacking/transition/visual-debug as
`@utility`, primitives as `@utility`, logos as `@declaration`) and want them under one **Plugins**
subsection of the CSS API, after Declarations. Today they land in a separate `"CSS plugins"` top-level
section.

#### Current behavior (for reference)

- `@cssdoc/markdown` `KIND_GROUPS` = `component→Components`, `utility→Utilities`, `rule→Rules`,
  `declaration→Declarations` (fixed order).
- `buildSidebar(entries, baseHref)` and `renderIndex(entries, options)` both iterate `KIND_GROUPS`,
  `filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, and drop empty groups. Grouping key is `entry.kind` only.
- `@group`/`@category` is already parsed to `CssDocEntry.group?: string`, but only drives the per-page
  `**Group:** <value>` meta line in `renderEntry` — never the sidebar or index.

#### Proposed change

Group by **`entry.group ?? kindLabel(entry.kind)`** in both `buildSidebar` and `renderIndex`:

- A record **with** `@group Foo` joins a group labelled `Foo` (leaving its kind group).
- A record **without** `@group` stays in its kind group — unchanged.
- **Group order:** the kind groups first, in `KIND_GROUPS` order (each holding only its ungrouped
  records), then any custom `@group` groups in **first-appearance order** (deterministic — `entries`
  are already name-sorted). So `@group Plugins` records form a `Plugins` group after `Declarations` with
  zero extra config — which is exactly the pantoken layout.
- Empty groups are still dropped.

Sketch (shared helper so sidebar and index stay identical):

```js
// @cssdoc/markdown
function groupEntries(entries) {
  const kindLabel = Object.fromEntries(KIND_GROUPS.map(g => [g.kind, g.label]));
  const order = [];                    // group labels in display order
  const byLabel = new Map();           // label -> entries[]
  const push = (label, e) => {
    if (!byLabel.has(label)) { byLabel.set(label, []); }
    byLabel.get(label).push(e);
  };
  for (const g of KIND_GROUPS) order.push(g.label);          // kind groups first
  for (const e of entries) push(e.group ?? kindLabel[e.kind], e);
  for (const label of byLabel.keys())                        // then custom groups, first-appearance
    if (!order.includes(label)) order.push(label);
  return order.filter(l => byLabel.has(label => l)).map(label => ({ label, entries: byLabel.get(label) }));
}
```

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` then iterate `groupEntries(entries)` instead of `KIND_GROUPS`.

#### Optional: explicit group order

For consumers who want to pin or interleave order (e.g. put a custom group between kind groups, or
rename), add a `render.groups?: readonly string[]` to `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` (mirroring the
existing `sectionOrder`), threaded through `EmitCssApiOptions` like `sectionOrder`/`structureView`
already are. Listed labels order first (in that order); unlisted groups append in the default order
above. Omitted → the default order. pantoken wouldn't need it (the default already yields
`…Declarations, Plugins`), but it makes the feature complete.

#### Backward compatibility

- Records without `@group` — **no change**.
- Records that already use `@group` today get sidebar/index grouping in addition to the existing
  `**Group:**` meta line. That's a behavior change for those records only. `@group` is niche and the new
  behavior is the tag's intuitive meaning, so we'd treat this as a minor release. If strict compatibility
  is preferred, gate it behind a `render.groupBy: "kind" | "group"` (default `"kind"`) — but we'd
  recommend making `@group` grouping the default.
- The per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line can stay as-is (harmless) or be dropped once the group is
  visible in the nav — maintainers' call; not required by this proposal.

#### Consumer example (pantoken)

With this change, pantoken collapses its two `emitCssApi` calls into one and tags each plugin record:

```css
/**
 * @utility stacking
 * @group Plugins
 * @summary z-index depth utilities…
 */
```

Result: a single `"CSS"` section → `Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`, with all
five plugin records (mixed kinds) under **Plugins**. No second section, no sidebar post-processing.

#### Alternative considered (and why we prefer the tag)

An emit-time option — `emitCssApi({ label: "CSS", group: "Plugins" })` that merges a call's records into
an existing section as one flat subgroup — would let a consumer keep separate `emitCssApi` calls (handy
when the groups need different `resolveSource`/`importSnippet`). But it changes `mergeCssSidebar` from
replace-by-label to merge-into-a-section, adds a "flat group" mode to `buildSidebar`, and is
per-call rather than per-record. The `@group` approach is smaller, reuses an existing tag and the
already-parsed `CssDocEntry.group`, and is authored where the record lives. We'd be happy with either;
the tag is our recommendation.

#### Touch points

- `@cssdoc/markdown`: `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex` (+ a shared `groupEntries` helper). Core change.
- `@cssdoc/config`: `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` — only if the optional `render.groups` is adopted.
- `@cssdoc/typedoc`: thread `groups`/`groupBy` through `EmitCssApiOptions` → `buildCssApi`, alongside the
  existing `sectionOrder`/`structureView` defaults — only if the optional config is adopted.
- No change needed to `@cssdoc/core` (`CssDocEntry.group` already exists) or `@cssdoc/spec`.

---

## Follow-up (pantoken, after cssdoc ships)

Once cssdoc honors `@group` for grouping:

1. Add `@group Plugins` to the five plugin records (in each `plugins/pantoken/*/scripts/generate.ts` doc
   block: stacking, transition, visual-debug, primitives, logos).
2. Collapse the two `emitCssApi` calls in `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` into one — feed the plugin
   sheets into the `css` array, merge `resolveSource`/`importSnippet` into name-keyed maps (record names
   don't collide), and widen the drift-guard allowlist to the plugin-local prefixes.
3. Delete the `css-plugins` `outSubdir`/`label` path; regenerate docs; re-run `docs:api:locales:claude`
   for the moved pages; browser-verify the CSS section shows `Components · Utilities · Rules ·
   Declarations · Plugins`.

## Verification (of the proposal deliverable)

- The proposal is a document — "verification" is accuracy: every cssdoc symbol it names
  (`KIND_GROUPS`, `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex`, `CssDocEntry.group`, `EmitCssApiOptions`,
  `mergeCssSidebar`, `RenderConfig`, `cssDocSchema`) was confirmed present in `@cssdoc/*@0.7.8` under
  `node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+*/dist/`.
- On approval: write the proposal to `docs/internal/proposals/cssdoc-custom-groups.md`; do not modify
  pantoken's docs pipeline yet (that's the post-ship follow-up).

### Proposal: group sidebar & index by `@group`, not only by record kind

**cssdoc version reviewed:** 0.7.8

#### Summary

Let CSS records opt into a named sidebar/index group via the existing `@group`/`@category` tag, instead
of always grouping by the four record kinds. Records without `@group` are unchanged. This is a small,
backward-compatible change in `@cssdoc/markdown`, and it removes the need for consumers to emit a second
top-level `emitCssApi` section (or post-process the sidebar) just to get a custom group.

#### Motivation

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` group records solely by `record.kind` via the hardcoded `KIND_GROUPS`
array. A consumer that wants an extra section — e.g. a **Plugins** group holding records of mixed kinds
(some `@utility`, some `@declaration`) — has no supported way to do it within one section. The only
workarounds are:

1. A **second `emitCssApi` call** with a different `label` → a separate *top-level* sidebar section
   (`mergeCssSidebar` keys on `label`), which is a sibling of the main CSS section, not a child of it.
2. **Post-processing the emitted `typedoc-sidebar.json`** to splice the second section's items back in as
   a subgroup — brittle and outside cssdoc's contract.

pantoken hits exactly this: we document five CSS-emitting plugins (stacking/transition/visual-debug as
`@utility`, primitives as `@utility`, logos as `@declaration`) and want them under one **Plugins**
subsection of the CSS API, after Declarations. Today they land in a separate `"CSS plugins"` top-level
section.

#### Current behavior (for reference)

- `@cssdoc/markdown` `KIND_GROUPS` = `component→Components`, `utility→Utilities`, `rule→Rules`,
  `declaration→Declarations` (fixed order).
- `buildSidebar(entries, baseHref)` and `renderIndex(entries, options)` both iterate `KIND_GROUPS`,
  `filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, and drop empty groups. Grouping key is `entry.kind` only.
- `@group`/`@category` is already parsed to `CssDocEntry.group?: string`, but only drives the per-page
  `**Group:** <value>` meta line in `renderEntry` — never the sidebar or index.

#### Proposed change

Group by **`entry.group ?? kindLabel(entry.kind)`** in both `buildSidebar` and `renderIndex`:

- A record **with** `@group Foo` joins a group labelled `Foo` (leaving its kind group).
- A record **without** `@group` stays in its kind group — unchanged.
- **Group order:** the kind groups first, in `KIND_GROUPS` order (each holding only its ungrouped
  records), then any custom `@group` groups in **first-appearance order** (deterministic — `entries`
  are already name-sorted). So `@group Plugins` records form a `Plugins` group after `Declarations` with
  zero extra config — which is exactly the pantoken layout.
- Empty groups are still dropped.

Sketch (shared helper so sidebar and index stay identical):

```js
// @cssdoc/markdown
function groupEntries(entries) {
  const kindLabel = Object.fromEntries(KIND_GROUPS.map(g => [g.kind, g.label]));
  const order = [];                    // group labels in display order
  const byLabel = new Map();           // label -> entries[]
  const push = (label, e) => {
    if (!byLabel.has(label)) { byLabel.set(label, []); }
    byLabel.get(label).push(e);
  };
  for (const g of KIND_GROUPS) order.push(g.label);          // kind groups first
  for (const e of entries) push(e.group ?? kindLabel[e.kind], e);
  for (const label of byLabel.keys())                        // then custom groups, first-appearance
    if (!order.includes(label)) order.push(label);
  return order.filter(l => byLabel.has(l)).map(l => ({ label: l, entries: byLabel.get(l) }));
}
```

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` then iterate `groupEntries(entries)` instead of `KIND_GROUPS`.

#### Optional: explicit group order

For consumers who want to pin or interleave order (e.g. put a custom group between kind groups, or
rename), add a `render.groups?: readonly string[]` to `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` (mirroring the
existing `sectionOrder`), threaded through `EmitCssApiOptions` like `sectionOrder`/`structureView`
already are. Listed labels order first (in that order); unlisted groups append in the default order
above. Omitted → the default order. pantoken wouldn't need it (the default already yields
`…Declarations, Plugins`), but it makes the feature complete.

#### Backward compatibility

- Records without `@group` — **no change**.
- Records that already use `@group` today get sidebar/index grouping in addition to the existing
  `**Group:**` meta line. That's a behavior change for those records only. `@group` is niche and the new
  behavior is the tag's intuitive meaning, so we'd treat this as a minor release. If strict compatibility
  is preferred, gate it behind a `render.groupBy: "kind" | "group"` (default `"kind"`) — but we'd
  recommend making `@group` grouping the default.
- The per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line can stay as-is (harmless) or be dropped once the group is
  visible in the nav — maintainers' call; not required by this proposal.

#### Consumer example (pantoken)

With this change, pantoken collapses its two `emitCssApi` calls into one and tags each plugin record:

```css
/**
 * @utility stacking
 * @group Plugins
 * @summary z-index depth utilities…
 */
```

Result: a single `"CSS"` section → `Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`, with all
five plugin records (mixed kinds) under **Plugins**. No second section, no sidebar post-processing.

#### Alternative considered (and why we prefer the tag)

An emit-time option — `emitCssApi({ label: "CSS", group: "Plugins" })` that merges a call's records into
an existing section as one flat subgroup — would let a consumer keep separate `emitCssApi` calls (handy
when the groups need different `resolveSource`/`importSnippet`). But it changes `mergeCssSidebar` from
replace-by-label to merge-into-a-section, adds a "flat group" mode to `buildSidebar`, and is
per-call rather than per-record. The `@group` approach is smaller, reuses an existing tag and the
already-parsed `CssDocEntry.group`, and is authored where the record lives. We'd be happy with either;
the tag is our recommendation.

#### Touch points

- `@cssdoc/markdown`: `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex` (+ a shared `groupEntries` helper). Core change.
- `@cssdoc/config`: `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` — only if the optional `render.groups` is adopted.
- `@cssdoc/typedoc`: thread `groups`/`groupBy` through `EmitCssApiOptions` → `buildCssApi`, alongside the
  existing `sectionOrder`/`structureView` defaults — only if the optional config is adopted.
- No change needed to `@cssdoc/core` (`CssDocEntry.group` already exists) or `@cssdoc/spec`.

Done — merged to main as PR [#11](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/11) (`4fa3e2b`).

## What landed

The plugin records now live **inside** the CSS API section as a Plugins subsection, using the cssdoc 0.7.9 `@group` feature — the exact design from our upstream proposal:

**CSS → Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins**

- **Tagged each plugin record `@group Plugins`** in the five `plugins/pantoken/*/scripts/generate.ts` blocks. 0.7.9 groups by `@group` (falling back to kind), so the five mixed-kind plugin records collapse into one group, ordered last.
- **Collapsed the two `emitCssApi` calls into one** in `build-css-api.ts` — plugin sheets join the single `"CSS"` section, `resolveSource`/`importSnippet` merged into name-keyed lookups, with an explicit `groups` order. Pages moved from `/api/css-plugins/*` to `/api/css/*`; the separate top-level section is gone.
- **hu translation** for the six changed blocks (each plugin page gained a `**Group:** Plugins` meta line); drift and parity green.

## Verified

- `vp check` clean; cssdoc lint accepts `@group`; the stale `css-plugins` tree is cleaned by TypeDoc.
- Browser-checked the live nav: the CSS section's children render as exactly `Overview · Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`, and `/api/css/stacking` shows `Group: Plugins` with the right `@import`.
- CI green. **No release needed** — the plugin `scripts/` aren't in the published package (only `dist`), and the minified dist sheets strip doc comments, so the npm artifacts are unchanged; everything else is docs/build tooling.

One nice outcome: because 0.7.9 shipped the proposal's default ordering (kinds first, then custom `@group` groups), the layout you wanted fell out without even needing the explicit `groups` option — I passed it anyway to make the intent self-documenting.
